text:
Sam K: quick heads-up — ran a short profiler against the new kernel selector on canary. observing intermittent p99 OOMs when serving long-context requests (>6k). looks like kernel handoff picks a lower-latency kernel that has a higher peak-workspace allocation, which fragments the recycler and delays buffer reuse. attaching short log snippet and a tiny selector excerpt.

Sam K: log:
```
[2026-03-10 14:02:11] request id=abc123 seq=8200 kernel=fast_attn_A inst_size=1.35GB alloc=1.36GB
[2026-03-10 14:02:11] recycler: free_pool=4 buffers=64 pending_reclaim=12
[2026-03-10 14:02:12] OOM: failed to allocate 1.2GB for decode window
```

Sam K: selector pseudocode that triggered it: 
```
if (predicted_tok_time_A < predicted_tok_time_B) return A;
else if (predicted_tok_time_B * 1.02 < predicted_tok_time_A) return B;
```
(doesn't consider peak_workspace)

Maya R: saw the same on the edge cluster yesterday. p95 fine, but p99 latency spikes then OOMs. looks correlated with batch splitting where some large requests are routed to the fast kernel. :thinking:

Jorge P: hypothesis: the selector only optimizes for throughput/latency, not peak memory. for mixed workloads that causes higher fragmentation. quick fix: prefer kernel with lower peak_workspace when predicted_seq_len > 4k.

Jorge P: suggested snippet to add: 
```
score = latency_cost + lambda * peak_workspace_estimate;
choose min(score)
```
lambda can be tunable per tier.

Alex L: +1. also we should add a per-request soft cap for workspace usage (e.g., cap_request_workspace = 1GB) so a single kernel choice can't starve the recycler. fallback to streaming/decode path if kernel would exceed cap. rollout plan:
- feature-flag the memory-aware selector (runtime flag)
- A/B 5% canary on staging -> 25% prod -> full rollout if no regressions
- metric: p99 latency, p99 memory per-gpu, OOM-rate, recycler_free_pool

ci-bot: perf-check results for fast_attn_A vs mem_saver_B on canary (last 24h):
- p50 latency: A=28ms B=34ms
- p99 latency: A=420ms B=460ms
- OOMs: A=6 events B=0 events
- token-cost delta: +3% for B
(note: numbers normalized)

Maya R: those ci numbers match what we saw. small latency hit but zero OOMs is attractive for tail-sensitive customers. recommend tuning lambda so we only pick B for >6k sequences.

Sam K: action items:
- Jorge: prototype memory-aware score and add peak_workspace estimator (small PR) — target eod Thu
- Alex: add per-request workspace soft-cap + runtime flag + canary config — target Mon
- Maya: run targeted canary on the long-context workload and collect recycler histograms — target Wed
- I'll add an alert for recycler_free_pool < 8 and OOM rate > 1/day to catch regressions.

Jorge P: one more observation — fragmentation increases when kernel swap happens mid-batch because buffers returned have different shapes. maybe co-locate similar kernels per-batch or prefer sticky kernel per-req to reduce churn.

Alex L: good point. sticky-kernel for duration of request sounds low-risk. we can enable for canary too.

Maya R: leaving a short repro (small script) in the perf bucket: s3://redwood-perf/long-context/kernel_handoff_repro.tar.gz

Sam K: thanks team. I'll open the tracking issue and link PRs. :rotating_light: prioritize on-call awareness for the canary rollout so we can abort fast if recycler/free_pool trends down.

Alex L: noted — I'll schedule a short standby for rollout.

ci-bot: deploy check: memory-aware-selector feature-flag created (ff/ms_selector_2026_03_10). canary config saved.
